comparison: Both evaluate YafK's hydrolytic activity and quantification of bond hydrolysis (C27, C36, C41, C42). OpenEval provides detailed technical support for the quantitative analysis, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the evidence as 'solid,' showing strong agreement on this core finding.

Both address the dynamic equilibrium and Lpp shuffling mechanism (C6, C32, C35, C48, C49). OpenEval emphasizes the demonstration of old free Lpp tethering to new PG and transbilayer movement, while peer reviewers explicitly validate that 'lpp molecules are shuffled on and off the peptidoglycan,' showing strong concordance.

Both address spatial independence of Lpp tethering from PG incorporation (C4, C19, C20, C21, C22, C44, C46). OpenEval provides detailed support based on isotopologue data, while peer reviewers implicitly support these findings through acceptance of the methodology and overall conclusions about attachment timing.

Both evaluate the speculative claim about limited septal Lpp incorporation (C5, C26). OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN, noting alternative explanations are not ruled out, while peer reviewers also express uncertainty, noting 'some of the other data still remain incomplete.' Both recognize the inferential nature of this claim.

Both address kinetic observations from comparative strain analysis (C19, C20, C27, C28, C30, C33, C39, C40). OpenEval supports the differential decay rates as evidence for YafK activity, while peer reviewers affirm the 'label-chase mass spectrometry experiments' and describe the evidence as solid, showing agreement on experimental validity.

Both evaluate isotopologue data supporting Lpp shuffling (C32, C33, C35, C39, C40). OpenEval supports the interpretation of new→old isotopologues as evidence of shuffling, while peer reviewers validate the overall experimental approach and molecular function findings, showing alignment.

Both address physiological implications regarding vesiculation (C52). OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN, noting the hypothesis requires experimental validation, while peer reviewers explicitly criticize the lack of physiological context and disagree with deferring OMV data. Both identify this as inadequately supported, though peer review is more critical.

OpenEval evaluates established background knowledge about bacterial cell envelope architecture, PG structure, and Lpp function (C1, C2, C61-C73). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel experimental findings rather than background material.

OpenEval evaluates established knowledge about LDT enzyme family and catalytic mechanisms (C7-C10, C74-C78). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as this represents background information rather than novel claims requiring peer validation.

OpenEval evaluates established knowledge about Lpp abundance, distribution, and function (C11-C16). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers did not separately assess this background material.

OpenEval evaluates prior findings about ΔyafK mutants from Bahadur et al., 2021 and Winkle et al., 2021 (C17, C18). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as this represents cited prior work rather than novel findings.

OpenEval evaluates the experimental methodology for isotope labeling (C53-C60). No corresponding peer review evaluation found as a separate item, though peer reviewers validated the overall experimental approach in their assessment of results.
